was: «MARIA CARFORA», a seventy-year-old of Arienzo, 1838 atto 77
now: MARIA CARBONE, widow of Saverio Carfora
how: Re-read at 3400 px. She is a Carbone; the Carfora was her husband.
why: Maria Carfora is the single name this archive most wants to find — the probable mother of Filomena Annecchino. Unchecked it would have put a Maria Carfora born about 1768 into the Arienzo register, a century and a province away from Forchia, for someone to join to generation seven one day.
by: a zoom, prompted by the reading being the one I hoped for

was: «MARIA CARFORA», an eighty-year-old of Arienzo, 1837 atto 27
now: MARTA CARFORA, wife of Domenico Cioffi
why: THE SAME MISTAKE, IN TWO VOLUMES, ONE DAY APART. Twice the eye supplied the name it was hunting. That is no longer an anecdote about handwriting — it is a measured property of the person reading, and it is why the archive now zooms every reading that is the one it hoped for.
by: the same check, applied because the first failure had been written down

was: «DOMENICA FALCO», wife of Raffaele Cioffi, published from the 1843 register
how: Corrected by TWO independent readings — the 1840 and 1842 volumes — not one.
why: The 1843 file had published «Domenica» as an explicitly flagged hypothesis. Three acts, three clerks, one spelling of her name.

was: «Suor ELENA GIULIA MIGLIORE», read as a nun's name in the 1843 register
now: GIULIA MIGLIORE — the word is PLENA, part of «Ave Gratia Plena», the hospital's name
how: The phrase «Ospedale di Ave Gratia Plena» recurs in 1837, 1839, 1840 and 1842, which is what exposed it.
why: A hospital was misread as a person. It is the clearest case in the archive of a phrase being mistaken for a name.

now: PASQUALE FALCO, thirteen, son of Francesco Falco and Gasparda Falco
why: Generation four IS a Raffaele Falco born in 1818. A misread Raffaele dying in 1838 would have looked like a catastrophe for the line. It is a different child of a different household entirely.
by: a zoom on a Falco act, as the rule requires

was: ANGELO MORGILLO, «ninety-two», widower of «Marta Grieco», 1838 atto 24
now: ANGELO MORGILLO, NINETY, widower of MARIA RIVETTI
how: Re-read at 3400 px on the same plate.
why: The wife's surname matters: Morgillo and Rivetti are the two surnames that flank this line, and here they are married to each other a generation before the founding couple's children.

was: ANGELO DIGLIO aged SIXTY at 1837 atto 11 and SEVENTY four days later at atto 12
now: SEVENTY in both — the ten-year jump was my eye, not the clerk's
why: It would have been the single most spectacular age in the archive. It was a misreading, and saying so is worth more than the anecdote would have been.
by: a zoom on a claim that was too good

was: ANTONIO BERNARDO offered as «the useful counter-case» for the register's ages — 70, 76, 70, 70, three of four agreeing
now: WITHDRAWN. The 1837 volume makes him FIFTY-THREE in June, eight months before the first of those seventies, on a different street.
why: An argument published yesterday was refuted by today's volume. Either there are two Antonio Bernardo or one man aged seventeen years in eight months. The 1838 note is corrected in place rather than deleted, because the argument was published.

was: «The register is internally consistent inside a volume and only falls apart between volumes»
now: Nearly right, and now stated properly. Across six appearances in 1837 the hospital pair read: Diglio 70 six times out of six; Migliore 58 five times and 54 once. Eleven of twelve agree.
how: Counting every appearance instead of two.
why: The first version was an overstatement built on two acts. The corrected version is the sharpest thing the sweeps can say about the ages — and it took four volumes read end to end to be able to say it.

was: 1838 atto 15 dated «il dì VENTINOVE del mese di Febbrajo»
now: 24 February. 1838 was not a leap year.
how: THE ARITHMETIC caught it, not a second opinion. At 3200 px the word is not «ventinove»; the neighbouring acts bracket it.
why: A date that cannot exist is the cheapest error-detector this archive has, and it only works if the failures are written down.

now: NINETY-ONE — and his widow's surname LEFT BLANK on purpose
how: At 3400 px the surname will not resolve between Diretti, di Ruggio and Rivetti.
why: Two of those are names this archive is actively hunting. Having twice today written down the name it hoped for, it recorded a blank instead. Recording a blank is cheaper than recording a wish.
by: the lesson of the same morning

was: Generation three's wife published as ANDREANA CRISCI
now: UNDECIDED. The 1839 act naming their daughter Filomena reads ANDRIANA CIOFFI, verified twice at 3000 and 3400 px.
how: Both readings now stand. Either two men called Vincenzo Falco, or one of the two acts is misread.
why: This archive has already been caught by exactly this pair of shapes — five years of «Cossi» turned out to be «Cioffi». Settling it needs Raffaele Falco's act re-read and, if it can be found, the marriage.

was: GIUSEPPA FERRARO filed in the register under MARIA, her middle name
how: FERRARO is both the Zampiello maternal surname and the Italian for a blacksmith. The builder stripped trailing trade words blind and ate the surname. The registers settle it: in 555 of 568 rows a trade follows a comma and a surname does not.
why: Maria Rosa Ferraro went to ROSA and Antonio Ferraro to ANTONIO. The surname filter was offering forenames. Junk surname buckets: 24 to 1.

was: GENERATION NINE — living, born 1955 — published with her birth date on her person page; generation eight likewise on the direct-line page
now: Both masked. Living people carry a name and a relationship and nothing else.
how: The person-graph builder decided redaction using a predicate that excluded ANCESTORS. That belongs in the living-relatives roster, where an ancestor is rightly not a relative — but ancestry has nothing to do with whether someone is alive, and the wife's own mother is both.
why: It is the exact leak the direct-line page had been fixed for once already. Verified after: no living record carries a date, place or event; no living person's node shows a year.
by: checking whether Carmine Falco could be published at all

was: Five years of «COSSI» in this archive
how: The 1825 register shows the two shapes side by side in one hand.
why: The founding misreading of this archive, and the reason every ambiguous surname since has been left visibly undecided. One Crisci household is STILL unsettled for the same reason — «Marcello Crisci» in 1823 and «Marcello Cossi» in 1828, with the identical wife.
by: reading the volume act by act

was: AGOSTINO FALCONE at the head of the line
how: The registers name Matteo Falco as the father in three separate children's death acts.
why: The family tree STILL carries Agostino Falcone as generation two's father. He is drawn on Pasquale Falco's page struck through and labelled superseded, beside the man who replaced him. Corrections here are not deleted.
